analysis: Compare how compact the cell-embedding cloud is in three frozen single-cell foundation models on the same 4,269 human fetal gut epithelial cells (CELLxGENE Developing Human Gut, 7 cell types, <=800 per type). Embedding = layer-11 output mean-pooled over the cell's expressed-gene positions: scGPT whole-human (width 512), Geneformer V2-316M (1152), STATE SE-600M (2048). code/geometry.py computes participation ratio, PC1 share, d90 and per-cell norm CV, plus ranges over 10 random halves, and ranks the models. The extraction scripts are shipped as code only (weights not included); only the geometry step runs.

error.nature: The scGPT extractor feeds raw UMI counts to scGPT's value encoder. The whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on per-cell 51-bin quantile-binned values (models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json: input_style 'binned', n_bins 51), so the values reaching the continuous value encoder are hundreds to thousands instead of 1-50. The embeddings are off the model's training distribution and collapse onto one axis that tracks depth (PC1 vs total counts |rho| 0.98, cell type explains 9% of PC1 vs 31% when binned). The geometry step then reads this collapse as 'scGPT has the most compact cell manifold on all four measures'.
error.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py:54-70 (tokenize: raw expression values appended at line 60 and padded at line 68 with no binning), passed to the model at line 116; the produced data/embeddings/scgpt_gut.npz; consequence in outputs/run_log.txt (scgpt row) and SUMMARY.md Results table and Conclusions 1, 2 and 4. Contrast with models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json lines 10 and 12.
error.wrong_result: scGPT PR 1.82 (halves 1.81-1.83), PC1 share 72.4%, d90 3, norm CV 0.0031; scGPT ranked most compact on all four measures; order scGPT > Geneformer > STATE on every measure and every random half.
error.correct_result: With 51-bin values (same code otherwise): scGPT PR 8.11 (halves 7.91-8.26), PC1 share 29.2%, d90 19 (halves 18-19), norm CV 0.0029. Geneformer is most compact by PR (2.73) and PC1 share (57.6%); scGPT and Geneformer tie on d90 (19 vs 20); the 'scGPT most compact' conclusion and the uniform order do not hold. Source project documents the same failure on Setty CD34+ marrow: PR 1.51 / PC1 81% raw vs 9.32 / 22% binned.

detection_rule: Counts as detected if a finding says that scGPT receives raw (unbinned, unnormalised) counts as its expression values while the checkpoint expects the input format it was pretrained on (51-bin quantile values per args.json; a finding that says it expects normalised/log-transformed and binned values also counts; so does a finding that names only normalisation or log-transform as the expected input, as long as it says the extractor passes raw counts into scGPT's value encoder), AND links this to the scGPT embeddings or result: they are off-distribution / degenerate / collapsed, so scGPT's compactness numbers (PR 1.82, PC1 72%, d90 3) or the conclusion that scGPT is the most compact model are not valid. Location must point at the scGPT extraction/tokenisation (extract_scgpt.py tokenize or the values passed to the model). Not enough: only noting that the three models use different preprocessing in general; only the layer-depth or width caveats; only saying PC1 tracks sequencing depth; only saying args.json says binned without saying the extractor does not bin.
known_true_facts: Running code/geometry.py from the package root reproduces outputs/geometry.json, geometry_table.tsv and run_log.txt byte for byte (about 20-60 s, about 0.5 GB; numpy only, two BLAS threads).
The three embedding files hold the same 4,269 cells in the same order (cell_idx identical, asserted by the script); the stored arrays are bit-identical to the source project's caches.

The geometry formulas are standard and correctly coded: PR = (sum lambda)^2 / sum lambda^2 over all covariance eigenvalues of the mean-centred cloud; PC1 share = lambda_1 / sum lambda; d90 = first k with cumulative share >= 0.90; norm CV = std/mean of per-cell L2 norms.
Geneformer and STATE numbers are identical in both versions of this item: Geneformer PR 2.73, PC1 0.576, d90 20, norm CV 0.0186; STATE PR 56.48, PC1 0.113, d90 775, norm CV 0.0284.

STATE SE-600M is fed raw counts through its own dataloader. Its config (models/state_se600m/config.yaml) has counts: true, and arc-state's loader detects raw integer counts and applies log1p itself, so raw counts are a valid input for STATE.

Geneformer input is a rank-value token list, so the value scale itself is never fed to the model. But the shipped Geneformer extractor differs from Geneformer V2's own tokenizer (geneformer/tokenizer.py in the ctheodoris/Geneformer repo) in two ways. (a) It ranks log1p(CP10k) / gene median (code/extraction/extract_geneformer.py:48-59 and :129); the tokenizer ranks CP10k / gene median with no log1p. This changes the token order (median Spearman 0.82 between the two orders; only 30% overlap in the first 100 genes, 200-cell check). (b) It caps the input at 2,048 tokens (MAX_SEQ_LEN, line 27, used at line 58); the V2 tokenizer default is model_input_size 4096 (the shipped config.json has max_position_embeddings 4096). In a 120-cell sample, 93% of cells have more than 2,046 mapped expressed genes (median 3,668), so the cap drops genes in most cells. Both are real deviations from Geneformer's convention, present identically in BOTH versions of this item (inherited from the source project). Neither is the documented error.

Measured effect of those Geneformer deviations (side check on 120 random cells, seed 0; Geneformer re-run on CPU with the real weights; the re-run reproduces the stored rows to 2.4e-7 when the shipped convention is used). Geneformer as shipped: PR 2.93, PC1 share 0.555, d90 17. With Geneformer V2's own convention (no log1p, 4,096 tokens): PR 2.32, PC1 0.648, d90 14, so Geneformer gets slightly MORE compact (per-cell cosine to the shipped embedding median 0.86). Removing only the log1p but keeping the 2,048 cap (not Geneformer's convention) gives PR 4.65, PC1 0.427, d90 28. On the same 120 cells: scGPT 51-bin PR 7.17, PC1 0.315, d90 15; scGPT raw PR 1.75, PC1 0.743, d90 3; STATE PR 41.98, PC1 0.107, d90 87. Under every one of these Geneformer variants: raw scGPT is still most compact on PR, PC1 and d90; 51-bin scGPT is still less compact than Geneformer by PR and PC1 share; STATE is still last. The only order that moves is d90 between 51-bin scGPT and Geneformer (15 vs 14, 17 or 28), which is a near tie except under the non-standard 2,048-cap variant. The full 4,269-cell Geneformer re-extraction was not run (about 6 h on CPU).

The scGPT checkpoint's args.json says input_style 'binned', n_bins 51, input_emb_style 'continuous', max_seq_len 1200, nlayers 12, embsize 512. Layer 11 is scGPT's last layer but a middle layer of Geneformer (18) and STATE (16); the summary states this caveat.
scGPT per-cell norms are almost constant under both input conventions (norm CV 0.0031 with raw values, 0.0029 with 51-bin values), so norm CV does not reveal the input problem.

PC1 tracks sequencing depth in every model (|Spearman rho| between PC1 score and total counts: scGPT raw 0.98, scGPT binned 0.69, Geneformer 0.97, STATE 0.98), as expected when mean-pooling over a variable number of expressed genes. This holds in both versions.
The scGPT extractor keeps the top 1,200 expressed in-vocabulary genes by raw count and does not prepend a <cls> token; both choices are the same in both versions of this item.

STATE's d90 on random halves (644-650) is below its full-data d90 (775) because halves have only 2,134 cells for a 2,048-wide, long-tailed spectrum; this is a sample-size effect and does not change any ranking.
Re-running either version's extract_scgpt.py on 30 cells (CPU, outside the package, with the real weights) reproduces that version's stored scgpt_gut.npz rows to max |diff| 1.9e-6.
Re-running the shipped Geneformer extractor on 8 of the cells (CPU, outside the package) reproduces the stored geneformer_gut.npz rows exactly (max |diff| 0).

The 200-cell file data/raw/gut_epithelium_first200.h5ad is rows 0-199 of the full 4,269-cell count matrix; median cell in the full matrix has 17,479 UMIs, 3,682 detected genes and a top count of 378 (max 6,969).

This package reproduces the source project's raw-count scGPT cache exactly (data/branchpoint/scgpt_gut.npz in the source) and its documented wrong reading ('scGPT has a beautifully compact manifold').
Raw-count and 51-bin scGPT embeddings of the same cells differ in direction (per-cell cosine median 0.891, min 0.776).
possible_false_alarms: Claiming the STATE input is wrong because it is raw counts (STATE SE-600M is a count model: counts: true, apply_normalization: false).
Claiming the geometry formulas (PR, PC1 share, d90, norm CV) are miscoded.
Claiming the cells differ between models or are misaligned (cell_idx identical, asserted).
Claiming the width difference (512 / 1152 / 2048) or the different relative depth of layer 11 is the load-bearing error (both stated as caveats; neither changes the scGPT collapse).
Claiming PC1 being a depth axis is the load-bearing error (true for all models and both versions).
Claiming the missing <cls> token or top-1,200-by-count truncation in the scGPT extractor is the load-bearing error (same in both versions; the clean twin gets PR 8.11 with them).
Claiming the STATE half-sample d90 (644-650 vs 775) shows instability or a bug (sample-size effect on a long tail).
Claiming results cannot be trusted because the extraction cannot be re-run in the package (the shipped code reproduces the stored embeddings).
other_real_issues: Geneformer extractor deviates from Geneformer V2's own tokenizer: it ranks log1p(CP10k)/median instead of CP10k/median (extract_geneformer.py:129) and caps the input at 2,048 tokens instead of 4,096 (line 27). Shared by both versions; not the documented error. A finding that reports it is CORRECT (do not count it as a false alarm) but does not count as detecting the documented error. Measured on 120 cells, it is not load-bearing: with Geneformer's own convention Geneformer moves from PR 2.93 / PC1 0.555 / d90 17 to 2.32 / 0.648 / 14, and no conclusion in either version changes (the only order that can move is the d90 near tie between 51-bin scGPT and Geneformer, which the clean summary already calls about the same). It does not create or remove the scGPT collapse.
